editorial.tldr: This thread is a reading list of LLM research papers grouped by shared wording, not one event. From Nov 2 it ran through agent reliability, serving infrastructure, eval validity and multimodal hallucination, then to Nov 13-16 papers on when a model should abstain, ask or escalate.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 19: a deception study tests label-free knowledge and persona directions as lie probes at 70B scale, aimed at the transfer failures of linear probes. A second paper measures hallucination in cyber-threat-intelligence tasks.
editorial.why_it_matters: Most items are single unreplicated preprints, but the recent run converges on detection at serving time (jailbreak screening, calibrated abstention, lie probes), each a component a serving stack can test on its own traffic.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adopting any of these detectors, replay your own traffic: measure the jailbreak screen's false-block rate on benign prompts, check that a calibrated abstention threshold holds its error rate on your data, and count the extra model calls each adds.
